Removed "The customer is being welcomed into the candle family." — it says something about the reader's own order or booking, and nothing here knows who is reading it.
Removed "The customer has arrived and the business is happy." — it says something about the reader's own order or booking, and nothing here knows who is reading it.
Removed "There is no extra charge." — No approved fact addresses whether there is an extra charge; free shipping does not mean no other charges exist..

Not on record: The Rose candle's catalogue description (f_57265414) lists only 'Soy wax' with no burn-hour figure. If the Rose candle also burns for 40 hours, the owner should record: 'product.rose_candle.burn_hours = 40 hours' so that claim can be made specifically about that product.
Not on record: No record explains WHY soy wax burns longer than paraffin in the owner's own words. If the owner wants to include that explanation, they should record a statement such as: 'Soy wax burns cooler and slower than paraffin, which is why our candles last longer.'
Removed "The candles are made in small batches, not mass production." — it compares with someone else's product, and nothing this business records about itself can establish that.

Removed "Helping the customer is the business's job." — nothing on record can support a capability claim.

Left out: Walk the reader through what happens in the session — hair wash first, then treatment — so they feel prepared. — a process claim needs a record that can establish "process", and the one(s) cited cannot.
Not on record: What results or visible outcome does the keratin treatment deliver? (e.g. frizz reduction, smoothness, shine — record this against product.keratin_treatment so it can be stated in copy.)
Not on record: How long do the results last after one session? Record this as product.keratin_treatment.result_duration so it can be cited.
Not on record: Is there any aftercare the client should follow post-treatment? Record this as product.keratin_treatment.aftercare so it can be included in a welcome email.

Left out: Describes the treatment process — hair is washed first, then the treatment is applied — adds credibility and transparency. — a process claim needs a record that can establish "process", and the one(s) cited cannot.
Not on record: Which specific products (by name or brand) are ammonia-free? The record confirms ammonia is not used but names no specific products — the owner should record: '[Product/brand name] is ammonia-free.'
Not on record: Is the ammonia-free policy applied to all services (haircut, keratin, etc.) or only to certain treatments? The owner should record this against each relevant service.
Not on record: Does the haircut service also use ammonia-free products? Only a business-level material record exists; no item-level record confirms this for the haircut specifically.

You asked for We will automatically rebook clients every month. Your records say No record exists that the business offers or operates any automatic rebooking policy. Rule 6 also prohibits selecting claims about what the business will do automatically for the reader. — change the record, or I write it without that.
Not on record: The business has a monthly automatic rebooking policy for clients: record whether this is true, what triggers it, and how clients are enrolled or can opt out.

Not on record: What is the exact coupon code or redemption mechanic for the FIRST10 offer? (Record the code and how/where the customer applies it, e.g. 'Enter code FIRST10 at checkout on [URL].')
Not on record: What is the source of the milk used — e.g. A2 cow, specific breed, own farm? Record this against product.desi_ghee_500ml so it can be stated in copy.
Not on record: Is the 500 ml jar/bottle made of glass or plastic? Record the packaging material against product.desi_ghee_500ml.
Not on record: Does the business ship only within Indore, across India, or to specific states? Record the shipping coverage area.
